newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs expect no good news on U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs expect no good news on U.S. CPI.

text.p: Belgian government bond (OLO) prices held broadly steady on Monday and dealers said the market would continue in a similar fashion at least until the 1230 GMT release of fresh U.S. indicators on Tuesday US-ECI.

March CPI data are forecast to show steady year-on-year and month-on-month headline rates, but a slight uptick in the core rate. "That would be more bad news," a trader said, noting much might already have been discounted.
"The market is cautious...on the negative side...there have been warnings from economists about the data...I expect some people to be on the short side," another said.
Another dealer said he saw no interest in the market and knew of no levels where buyers might emerge. "We thought six percent might spark some interest, but there was little there."

The benchmark 2007 OLO 26 BE286= yielded 6.06 percent at 1520 GMT, up from 6.02 percent late on Friday. It briefly dipped below six percent last week. One trader noted there had been some arbitraging between OLO 26 and Bunds.
Some players expect buying to emerge at around 6.10 percent.
Dealers said strong U.S. CPI numbers would reinforce expectations of another hike in Fed funds, this time in May.
Separately, after 1500 GMT, the Treasury will announce the OLO lines to be offered in its regular auction on April 21. The value date is April 24 BELK.
But it was by no means certain there would be a sell-off after such figures with the market already pricing in an increase in Fed funds by 50 to 75 basis points.
The only other feature on the Belgian market will be Tuesday's OLO exchange auction.

The Treasury is offering OLO line 4 (9.25 pct, Jan 1998) against OLO 13 (7.00 pct, April 1999), 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct March 2007) BELE.
Interest would centre on demand for OLO 26, the current 10-year benchmark.
